renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: lane_composition
  title: Share of each lane per library
  description: |-
    Each bar is a lane, split into the libraries of the sample sheet and the Undetermined reads, sized by their share of the lane. It answers how evenly the libraries share a lane and how much went unassigned.
    How to read: libraries pooled in equal amounts should take similar slices. A very large or very small slice points to a pooling imbalance, and a large Undetermined slice points to a sample sheet or index problem, so open the unknown barcodes tile next.
    Note: the eight largest libraries are drawn and the rest are grouped as Other.
  kind: stacked_bar
  config:
    top_n: 8
    x_title: Lane
    value_title: Share of the lane (%)
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    sample_id: lane_label
    taxon: sample
    rank: level
    abundance: pct_of_lane

- component: advanced_viz
  id: lane_sunburst
  title: Lanes and libraries by reads
  description: |-
    Each ring segment is a lane in the inner ring and a library in the outer ring, sized by its reads. It answers how the reads of the run split between lanes and, within a lane, between libraries.
    How to read: a lane with a much smaller arc than the others yielded fewer reads, and a library with a thin arc received little of its lane. The Undetermined reads appear as a segment of their own, so a large one points to a demultiplexing problem.
  kind: sunburst
  roles:
    abundance: reads
    ranks:
    - lane_label
    - sample

- component: advanced_viz
  id: library_index_purity
  title: Index purity against reads per library
  description: |-
    Each point is a library: its reads on the horizontal axis and the percentage of its reads whose index matched perfectly on the vertical axis, coloured by lane. It answers whether libraries with few reads are also the ones with doubtful index matches.
    How to read: libraries high on the axis are well assigned. A library low on the axis relies on reads with a mismatched index, which are more likely to come from a neighbouring sample, so check the unknown barcodes and the sample sheet for it. A library with very few reads is more exposed, since a few misassigned reads weigh more.
    Note: no cut-off is drawn, because the expected share depends on the library preparation and the instrument.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median share of reads with a perfect index match of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of bcl2fastq.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
    x_title: Reads
    y_title: Reads with a perfect index match (%)
    top_n_labels: 5
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    x: reads
    y: pct_perfect_index
    label: sample
    color: lane_label

- component: figure
  title: Share of the lane per library
  description: |-
    Each bar is a library, sized by its share of the lane's reads and coloured by lane. It answers which libraries are over or under represented in their lane.
    How to read: libraries pooled equally should have bars of similar height. A short bar marks a library that received few reads and may need resequencing, and a very tall one may be over pooled.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: sample
    y: pct_of_lane
    color: lane_label
    labels:
      sample: Library
      pct_of_lane: Share of the lane (%)
      lane_label: Lane

- component: card
  title: Reads in the largest libraries
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of reads over the rows in view, and the bars rank the libraries that hold the most. It answers how many reads the run produced and which libraries took the largest share.
    How to read: a library far above the others is over pooled. The total includes the Undetermined reads, so compare it with the lane health tile.
  column: reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: sample
  top_n_count: 3
  caption: the three libraries with the most reads, with the median and largest per row

- component: card
  title: Library share of the lane
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median share of a lane held by a library, and the box shows the quartiles over libraries. It answers how even the pooling is.
    How to read: a narrow box means even pooling, and a long whisker marks libraries well above or below the typical share. The median depends on the number of libraries in the lane.
  column: pct_of_lane
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread across libraries

- component: card
  title: Bases at Q30 or above
  description: |-
    The hero number is the median percentage of bases with a quality score of at least Q30, over the libraries in view, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how good the base calls are.
    How to read: a higher percentage is better, and a library well below the others points to a problem with its cluster density, chemistry or index. No cut-off is drawn, because the expected value depends on the instrument and read length. Open the read quality tile to see which read is worse.
  column: pct_q30
  aggregation: median
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: median, with its spread across libraries

- component: table
  title: Library demultiplexing table
  description: |-
    Each row is a library in a lane, or the Undetermined reads, with its index, its reads, its share of the lane, its yield, its Q30 share, its mean quality and the percentage of reads that matched the index perfectly or with one mismatch. It answers how each library was demultiplexed.
    How to read: sort by share of the lane or by index purity to find the libraries that need attention, and filter on a lane.

- component: advanced_viz
  id: lane_health
  title: Lane quality against Undetermined share
  description: |-
    Each point is a lane: the share of its reads that were Undetermined on the horizontal axis and the share of its bases at Q30 or above on the vertical axis, sized by yield and coloured by flowcell. It answers which lanes are healthy.
    How to read: a healthy lane sits in the upper left, with high quality and few unassigned reads. A lane to the right has many reads that no index matched, and a lane low on the axis has poor base quality, so open the unknown barcodes and read quality tiles for the lane. With few lanes, read the table instead.
    Note: no cut-off is drawn, because the expected values depend on the instrument and the library type.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median share of bases at Q30 or above of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of bcl2fastq.
  kind: scatter_xy
  config:
    reference_line: horizontal
    reference_stat: median
    x_title: Undetermined reads (%)
    y_title: Bases at Q30 or above (%)
    top_n_labels: 8
    legend_pos: bottom
  roles:
    x: pct_undetermined
    y: pct_q30
    label: lane_label
    size: yield_gb
    color: flowcell

- component: figure
  title: Yield per lane
  description: |-
    Each bar is a lane, sized by its yield in gigabases and coloured by flowcell. It answers whether the lanes produced similar amounts of data.
    How to read: lanes of one flowcell are expected to yield similar amounts, so a short bar points to a lane with a cluster, loading or instrument problem. Compare it with the clusters passing filter.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median yield per lane of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of bcl2fastq.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: lane_label
    y: yield_gb
    color: flowcell
    barmode: group
    labels:
      lane_label: Lane
      yield_gb: Yield (Gb)
      flowcell: Flowcell
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: yield_gb

- component: card
  title: Total yield
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total yield in gigabases over the lanes in view, and the bars rank the lanes. It answers how much data the run produced and how it divides between lanes.
    How to read: bars of similar length mean balanced lanes, and one much shorter bar points to a failing lane.
  column: yield_gb
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: lane_label
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: the lanes with the highest yield, with the median and largest per lane

- component: card
  title: Clusters passing filter
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of clusters that passed the instrument's purity filter over the lanes in view, and the bars rank the lanes. It answers how many clusters yielded usable reads.
    How to read: a lane with far fewer clusters than the others is under loaded or had a clustering problem. Compare it with the share of clusters passing filter in the table.
  column: clusters_pf
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - min
  - max
  secondary_layout: top_n
  breakdown_col: lane_label
  top_n_count: 4
  caption: the lanes with the most clusters, with the smallest and largest per lane

- component: card
  title: Lowest Q30 share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest percentage of bases at Q30 or above among the lanes in view, and the box shows the quartiles over lanes. It answers how good the worst lane is.
    How to read: a minimum far below the box marks a lane to investigate. No cut-off is drawn, because the expected value depends on the instrument and read length.
  column: pct_q30
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: the worst lane, with the spread over lanes

- component: card
  title: Highest Undetermined share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the highest share of reads left Undetermined among the lanes in view, and the box shows the quartiles over lanes. It answers how much data the worst lane lost to unassigned indexes.
    How to read: a maximum far above the box marks a lane to open in the unknown barcodes tile, where a sample sheet error or an index hop shows up. No cut-off is drawn, because the expected value depends on the library and the run.
  column: pct_undetermined
  aggregation: max
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: the worst lane, with the spread over lanes

- component: table
  title: Lane table
  description: |-
    Each row is a lane, with its clusters and those passing filter, its yield, its Q30 share, its mean quality, the number of libraries, the Undetermined share and how evenly libraries split the lane. It answers the run health lane by lane.
    How to read: sort by Undetermined share or by Q30 to find the lanes to check.

outputs.name: Base quality per lane and read

renders._yaml:
- component: advanced_viz
  id: lane_read_dots
  title: Base quality per lane and read
  description: |-
    Each dot is a read of a lane: its colour is the mean base quality and its size is the fraction of bases at Q30 or above. It answers which reads of which lanes have the best and worst quality.
    How to read: large dark dots are good. Read 2 is often lower than read 1 because quality falls along the cycles of paired-end runs, and a read much worse than its neighbours points to a chemistry or flowcell problem. Compare the lanes of a flowcell.
    Note: the Undetermined reads are pooled with the libraries here, so a lane with many Undetermined reads is averaged over both.
  kind: dot_plot
  roles:
    cluster: lane_label
    gene: read_label
    mean_expression: mean_quality
    frac_expressing: frac_q30

- component: figure
  title: Bases at Q30 or above per lane and read
  description: |-
    Each bar is a read of a lane, sized by its share of bases at Q30 or above and coloured by read. It answers how the quality compares between the reads and lanes.
    How to read: higher is better. A bar clearly shorter than the others marks a read or lane to investigate, and a gap between read 1 and read 2 is common in paired-end data. No cut-off is drawn, because the expected value depends on the instrument and read length.
    Lines and annotations: the dashed line is the median share of bases at Q30 or above of this table, a reference computed from the rows on show (it follows the filters), not a cut-off of bcl2fastq.
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: lane_label
    y: pct_q30
    color: read_label
    barmode: group
    labels:
      lane_label: Lane
      pct_q30: Bases at Q30 or above (%)
      read_label: Read
  reference_lines:
  - axis: y
    stat: median
    column: pct_q30

- component: card
  title: Lowest Q30 share
  description: |-
    The hero number is the lowest percentage of bases at Q30 or above among the reads and lanes in view, and the box shows the quartiles. It answers how good the worst read is.
    How to read: a minimum far below the box marks the read to check first. No cut-off is drawn, because the expected value depends on the instrument and read length.
  column: pct_q30
  aggregation: min
  aggregations:
  - box_plot_stats
  secondary_layout: box_plot
  caption: the worst read, with the spread over reads

- component: table
  title: Read quality table
  description: |-
    Each row is a read of a lane, with its yield, its Q30 share, the fraction at Q30 and its mean quality. It answers the quality read by read.
    How to read: sort by Q30 share to find the worst reads.

- component: figure
  title: Most frequent unknown barcodes
  description: |-
    Each bar is an index pair that bcl2fastq could not assign to a library, sized by its share of the lane and coloured by whether its indexes belong to libraries of the lane, one panel per lane. It answers what the unassigned reads are.
    How to read: a pair whose two indexes are both in use points to index hopping or a swap in the sample sheet, and a pair with only one index in use suggests a sequencing error or a mislabelled index. A pair with neither index in use suggests a library missing from the sheet. Index swapping is a known effect of patterned flow cells.
    Source: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/29739332/
  visu_type: bar
  dict_kwargs:
    x: barcode
    y: pct_of_lane
    color: swap_class
    facet_col: lane_label
    facet_col_wrap: 2
    labels:
      barcode: Index pair
      pct_of_lane: Share of the lane (%)
      swap_class: Index status
      lane_label: Lane

- component: card
  title: Unknown reads by index status
  description: |-
    The hero number is the total of reads in the listed unknown barcodes, and the ring splits them by whether their indexes are in use. It answers which cause is behind the unassigned reads.
    How to read: a ring dominated by pairs with both indexes in use points to hopping or a sheet swap, and one dominated by pairs with no index in use points to a missing library. Only the most frequent barcodes of each lane are listed, so the total is a part of the Undetermined reads.
  column: reads
  aggregation: sum
  aggregations:
  - median
  - max
  secondary_layout: donut
  breakdown_col: swap_class
  caption: split by status, with the median and largest per barcode

- component: table
  title: Unknown barcode table
  description: |-
    Each row is an unknown index pair of a lane, with its reads, its rank, its share of the lane and of the Undetermined reads, and whether each index belongs to a library of the lane. It answers which barcodes explain the unassigned reads.
    How to read: sort by rank and filter on the index status to find a swap candidate, then check the sample sheet for the pair.
